title: Dynamic Error Types
goal: Use Box<dyn Error> to return multiple distinct error types from one function.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Error Handling

sections.text: When writing application logic, functions often encounter different error types that do not share a common enum.

sections.caption: Box<dyn Error> erases concrete error types.

sections.text: `Box<dyn Error>` is a trait object that can hold any error implementing `std::error::Error`.
The `?` operator automatically boxes errors when the function return type is `Result<T, Box<dyn Error>>`.

sections.caption: Main returning dynamic error allows standard try operator usage.

sections.text: This simplifies application code but makes error matching harder for callers.

explanation: Use Box<dyn Error> to return multiple distinct error types from one function.
